Changing it to `<= width` lets a word join the current line when the result is exactly `width` characters, matching the documented behavior ("a line may be exactly `width` long").

arguments.summary: Fixed off-by-one in wrapper/wrap.py: the greedy join condition `len(current) + 1 + len(word) < width` was changed to `<= width`, so a word that fills the line to exactly `width` characters now joins the current line (e.g. wrap("aaa bbb", 7) → ["aaa bbb"]) instead of being pushed to a new line.
